items.title: MARKET PULSE AM OCT 9, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened mixed on Friday ahead of the tabling of 2027 Budget today, despite overnight losses on Wall Street. Dagang NeXchange Bhd emerged as the most actively traded stock after the company and CGP Fund resolved their long-running shareholder dispute over SilTerra Malaysia Sdn Bhd. IA5cGrMPGAY © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Iranian stuntwomen breaking gender norms with daring feats
items.summary: TEHERAN: As evening falls at a Teheran skatepark, a woman calmly steps forward with her body ablaze, performing a daring stunt that challenges convention in front of an impressed Iranian audience. Behind her, young women practise backward flips into a pit filled with foam, following the instructions of Nasrin Teymouri. In her thirties, she leads Iran's sole all-female stunt crew, a vital area of filmmaking traditionally controlled by men, but where Iranian women are increasingly establishing themselves.

items.title: Remand extended: Teen suspect held six more days over murder of classmate Irene Sofiya in Yong Peng
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 9 — The remand of a 16-year-old boy suspected of murdering a female student at a school in Yong Peng has been extended by six days, from tomorrow until Oct 15. The extension was granted by Magistrate Aimi Nawwar Mohamad Othman at the Magistrate’s Court here today. The teenager had previously been remanded for six days from Oct 4 to assist in the investigation into the death of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16.

items.title: 521kg meth seized from jet in Laos declared as vape products to conceal drugs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 521kg of crystal methamphetamine seized from a private jet in Laos was declared as vape products in the aircraft's cargo manifest to conceal the illicit shipment bound for Manila. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations revealed that the private jet initially departed Subang Airport without any cargo before arriving in Laos. He said the drugs were believed to have been loaded onto the aircraft in Laos for onward transport to Manila.

items.title: ‘I didn’t attack Nhaveen’: Accused tells High Court fight started with blow to friend’s face
items.summary: J. Ragesuthen, 27, told the High Court here that he was on Jalan Kaki Bukit when a “scuffle” occurred between his friend — who was another accused and a minor at the time of the incident — and T. Previin, who was Nhaveen’s friend. “I saw Previin hit another accused friend in the face with a helmet, and he passed out at the scene. Ragesuthen said he, Gokulan, and another accused helped carry the injured accused back home to get treatment.

items.title: Filipino suspected of masterminding Laos crystal meth smuggling plot
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Filipino is believed to have masterminded an attempt to smuggle more than half a tonne of crystal methamphetamine from Laos to Manila on a private jet linked to a Malaysian-operated aviation company. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said preliminary investigations found that the individual had arranged to charter the aircraft for US$49,500 (RM202,250) to transport goods from Laos to the Philippines. He said Malaysian police had shared information about the individual with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency to help trace and arrest the suspect.

items.title: Haze worsens with 37 areas recording unhealthy API levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions are worsening, with the number of areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings rising from 36 to 37 today. In the Klang Valley, Shah Alam recorded an API reading of 178. Putrajaya also recorded an API reading of 170.

items.title: Win-win for Petronas, Petros must pass commercial test
items.summary: Samirul Ariff Othman from Global Asia Consulting was responding to Sarawak senator Datuk Ahmad Ibrahim’s statement that commercial considerations involving Petronas cannot override Sarawak’s constitutional rights. Ahmad was rebutting former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim, who warned that Petronas could lose billions in business if Petros assumes a larger role in Sarawak’s gas sector. Abang Johari subsequently described the arrangement as a “win-win” for Petros and Petronas, saying it preserved Petronas’s existing role while recognising Petros as gas aggregator.

items.title: Retired JKR man killed as Proton Wira veers into opposite lane, collides head‑on with Persona in Setiu
items.summary: BANDAR PERMAISURI, Oct 9 — An elderly man was killed after the Proton Wira he was driving collided with a Proton Persona at Kilometre 44 of Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kota Bharu near Sungai Tong yesterday. The victim, identified as Zulkefli Daud, 72, a retired Public Works Department (JKR) employee from Kampung Jeli Seberang, Jeli, Kelantan, died while being taken to hospital. Setiu police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said the accident occurred at about 5.30pm and was believed to have happened when the victim’s car suddenly veered into the opposite lane.

items.title: New York City man shot by ICE agents with child in car
items.summary: NEW YORK: US immigration agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday while he was in his car with a child in the Marble Hill neighbourhood of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitnesses. "Early reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a 5-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds," New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement. "During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured," DHS said, adding that ICE officers rendered immediate aid.

items.title: Asia races to stockpile oil, speed up renewables in response to Iran war
items.summary: ASIAN countries are racing to raise their oil stockpiling capacity, complete a regional power grid and speed up renewables in response to supply risks laid bare by the Iran war. "The most advanced efforts are support for the development of oil stockpiling systems in each country and regional joint stockpiling on (a) voluntary basis," nine Southeast Asian nations said in a joint statement issued along with Japan and Australia. The Asean member countries also pledged to increase the share of clean energy in power generation, targeting 30 per cent renewables in total primary energy supply and 45 per cent in installed power capacity.

items.title: Nvidia-backed Firmus scraps US$5bil Australian IPO on poor demand
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia's Firmus, a data centre operator backed by Nvidia, shelved its US$5 billion initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions, and said it would opt for a private fundraising round instead. Firmus' IPO would have been the second-largest new share sale in Australia's history but met lukewarm demand, a warning sign that investors remain selective about AI issuers even as the artificial intelligence boom drives global markets. Its draft prospectus said it would make US$5 billion in annual earnings within five years from the data centres.

items.title: Mexico prison brawl leaves 10 dead
items.summary: MAZATLAN: Ten people were killed and more than a dozen injured after a fight broke out at a prison in Mexico's Sinaloa state on Thursday, the local government said. The Sinaloa Public Security Secretariat said on X that "a brawl occurred inside the prison facilities", without providing further details on what led to the violence. Sinaloa state in north-western Mexico has become a battleground for warring factions of the Sinaloa drug-trafficking cartel.

items.title: Food Act overhaul: Online sales, pesticide residues and unsafe packaging now under tighter watch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Dewan Rakyat yesterday passed the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 to strengthen food safety and quality controls and provide more comprehensive protection for consumers nationwide. The amendments to the Food Act 1983 (Act 281), the first comprehensive review of the act, include higher penalties, controls on samples of food contact materials (FCMs), monitoring of online food sales and monitoring of pesticide residue levels in agricultural produce. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the higher penalties were not intended to burden food operators or small traders, but to serve as a deterrent and safeguard public health.

items.title: Euro skids toward fifth weekly fall but selling pressure slows
items.summary: SINGAPORE: The euro was headed for a fifth straight weekly drop on Friday, though there were signs the selling streak was losing momentum as France's tumbling debt market stabilised and a decline in US yields took some steam out of the dollar's rally. The common currency had hit a 17-month low of US$1.1161 on Monday on market worries about France's record high debt load and the difficult political path to budget cuts, in contrast with a robust-looking US dollar and US economy. It has since recovered to trade at US$1.1211, for a fall this week of 0.3 per cent and a five-week drop of more than three per cent on the dollar.

items.title: Gold rises on softer dollar, easing yields; Fed outlook in focus
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.9 per cent to US$4,169.32 per ounce by 0137 GMT after hitting a two-month low on Wednesday. US gold futures gained 0.9 per cent to US$4,194.40. Spot silver rose 1.1 per cent to US$60.00, platinum gained 2.2 per cent to US$1,670.15 and palladium climbed 2.1 per cent to US$1,146.98.

items.title: Japan's Nikkei falls as AI doubts, bond stress weigh
items.summary: The broader Topix slipped 0.24 per cent to 4,081.62. Data on Friday showed Japan's August household spending fell 3.1 per cent year-on-year, underscoring cautious consumer sentiment and persistent inflation pressures. Furukawa Electric fell 4.83 per cent, followed by Murata Manufacturing, which lost 4.68 per cent.

items.title: Tech stocks struggle on AI spending worries, elevated yields
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Asian stocks slipped on Friday and were poised for a second straight weekly drop as investors fretted about elevated energy prices, bond market ructions and the huge sums needed to fund AI investment. President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US will not launch an attack on Iran before November's US midterm elections, although traders remained sceptical of any progress being made to end the war. "The big question for markets is whether Trump sticks to his word if Iranian attacks intensify," said Nick Twidale, chief market strategist at ATFX Global.

items.title: 2027 Budget to ensure national progress benefits all, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget reaffirms the government's commitment to ensuring that national progress benefits all Malaysians through continued improvements in their standard of living, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a post on X, Anwar said the fifth Madani Budget also prioritised the people's well-being and their ability to live with dignity. He urged the public to watch the live tabling of the 2027 Budget on major television channels and digital platforms at 3.30pm today.

items.title: Egypt president to make two-day state visit to Malaysia from Oct 9
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Egypt President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi will undertake a two-day state visit to Malaysia starting today at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia. "Malaysia and Egypt established diplomatic relations in 1959. Malaysia's total trade with Egypt was valued at RM3.08 billion (US$0.72 billion), with exports at RM2.55 billion (US$0.60 billion) and imports at RM0.53 billion (US$0.12 billion).

items.title: Tawau police arrest 14 boys after playground fight with weapons goes viral on social media
items.summary: TAWAU, Oct 9 — Police arrested 14 male students yesterday in connection with a group student fight involving weapons at the Taman Ambar Playground, Jalan Kuhara here last Monday. Tawau District Police Chief ACP Rosdi Mat Jusoh said the Criminal Investigation Division of the Tawau District Police Headquarters detained the suspects, aged between 12 and 14, to assist with the investigation. “Police received a report regarding the fight at 6pm last Monday.

items.title: Father recalls heartbreaking scene of daughter, grandchildren's fatal crash
items.summary: TANJONG KARANG: A father is struggling to come to terms with the loss of his eldest daughter and two grandchildren in a road crash involving a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) and a lorry at Bukit Talang, Jalan Raja Musa, yesterday. Mat Talpi Salamat, 72, said he rushed to the scene after receiving a call from his fifth child, Norhaslinda, 34, informing him that his eldest daughter, Norawalysa, 44, had been involved in the crash at about 1.30pm. he said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Malaysia retains Tier 2 ranking in US human trafficking report for third year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has retained its Tier 2 ranking in the 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report released by the United States Department of State, marking the third consecutive year it has held the rating. The Home Ministry said the ranking reflected continued international recognition of Malaysia's sustained efforts to combat human trafficking. The report acknowledged the country's progress, including stronger law enforcement, prosecutions of public officials complicit in trafficking crimes and increased government funding for anti-trafficking operations.

items.title: PTPTN borrowers can negotiate loan restructuring, deferment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Borrowers struggling to repay their National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loans can negotiate a repayment restructuring or apply for a deferment. The Higher Education Ministry said the government recognised the financial difficulties faced by borrowers genuinely struggling to settle their debts. "As of Aug 31, 2026, PTPTN's loan repayment arrears stood at RM10.7 billion, involving 1.16 million borrowers," the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply.

items.title: Struggling with PTPTN? MoHE says come talk — restructure, defer, and keep repayments on track
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Borrowers facing difficulties settling their National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loan arrears are welcomed to come forward to negotiate for loan restructuring or apply for deferment according to permitted flexibilities. The Ministry of Higher Education (MoHE), via a written reply published on the Parliament website yesterday, stated that the government is always mindful of the constraints faced by borrowers who are genuinely burdened in settling their loans. “The total loan repayment arrears for the agency reached RM10.7 billion involving 1.16 million borrowers as of August 31, 2026,” according to the ministry.

items.title: Selangor religious schools closed due to haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All religious schools under the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) will close from today due to the haze. "Private Islamic schools registered with JAIS are advised to follow this directive. Earlier, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said schools in four states , Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as Rompin district in Pahang, would be closed due to deteriorating haze conditions.

items.title: 12 politicians involved in 19 cases granted DNAA since 2010
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nineteen cases involving 12 politicians were granted a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) in the High Court and lower courts nationwide between 2010 and July this year. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the figures were based on information from the Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court and a review of criminal case records. She said, unlike civil cases, criminal cases were not subject to a limitation period, meaning individuals granted a DNAA could still be charged again with the same offences.

items.title: Budget 2027 aims to sustain growth while protecting households from subsidy reforms and cost pressures
items.summary: The 5th Madani Budget, themed “Malaysia Madani: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi”, is the second Budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP). The Budget comes at a time when the government seeks to sustain economic momentum while raising the nation’s growth ceiling, improving living standards and strengthening governance. Against this backdrop, fiscal policy will remain crucial in supporting economic growth while strengthening fiscal resilience, particularly amid external uncertainties, elevated energy costs and persistent cost pressures.

items.title: ‘Clean air not a luxury’: Manufacturers in Malaysia demand Asean accelerate haze-free roadmap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) has pressed for decisive, measurable regional action from Asean to eliminate transboundary haze, warning that recurring pollution inflicts severe damage on public health, worker safety, and economic productivity. In a statement today, FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok stressed that industrial and economic expansion must not come at the expense of environmental sustainability. While acknowledging existing regional frameworks, including the 2003 Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution and the Asean Haze-Free Roadmap 2023-2030, FMM stressed that member states must shift from diplomatic consensus to rapid, verifiable execution.

items.title: Anwar to table Budget 2027 today, promising resilience, reforms and relief for Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, is scheduled to table Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat at 3.30pm today. The tabling will be the fifth budget under his Madani Government, anchored by a clear commitment to ensure high value growth is translated equitably for the people’s wellbeing while strengthening the country’s economic resilience. The Budget 2027 tabling will be broadcast live on various local television stations and social media platforms, including Bernama TV, which will also air its Budget 2027 Analysis programme at 8.30pm tonight.

items.title: Haze: Penang schools remain open, outdoor activities suspended
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang schools will continue operating as usual, but all outdoor activities must be postponed amid the haze, said the state Education Department. The department said it was monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings around the clock across four stations in Minden, Seberang Jaya, Seberang Prai, and Balik Pulau. However, all outdoor activities must be postponed," it said.

items.title: Nationwide haze disruption: Fadhlina says schools in six states closed, others continue operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — All schools in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, and Selangor, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, alongside the Rompin district in Pahang, will close today due to the haze. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said school operations in other states, namely Perlis, Perak, Penang, Sabah, Sarawak, and Labuan, will proceed as usual. Earlier, the Negeri Sembilan Education Department (JPNS) announced the closure of all schools in the state based on Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at three monitoring stations, Port Dickson, Seremban, and Nilai, as of 5pm.

items.title: No haze respite: Seven spots exceed API of 180, no location in Malaysia with ‘Good’ air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Air quality remained at unhealthy levels across broad swathes of Malaysia this morning, prompting the closure of all schools in Selangor, Melaka, and Negeri Sembilan as Seremban logged the nation’s highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 186. According to Department of Environment (DOE) surveillance data as of 8.30am, 38 out of 68 monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality (API 101 to 200). None of the stations recorded good air quality, 30 registered moderate levels, and none breached the very unhealthy benchmark of 201.

items.title: Melaka Education Department confirms closures as haze worsens, teachers and parents urged to stay alert
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 9 — All schools under the Education Ministry in Melaka will be closed today, the Melaka Education Department said. The department said the decision was taken following monitoring and the Environmental Department’s official report showing the Air Pollution Index readings in major areas in Melaka had exceeded 150 and were at unhealthy levels. The Melaka education department and district education offices in Melaka Tengah, Jasin and Alor Gajah districts will continue to monitor the haze according to guidelines set by the Education Ministry,” the department said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: RM3,100 salary for singles in KL — baseline or comfortable?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A monthly salary of about RM3,100 for a single person in Kuala Lumpur should be seen as a financial baseline for a reasonable standard of living, not a guarantee of financial comfort. Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) Faculty of Human Ecology dean and personal financial planning lecturer Prof Dr Mohamad Fazli Sabri said the figure could serve as a benchmark for assessing whether a person could meet basic needs while setting aside some savings and preparing for emergencies. Fazli said income adequacy should not be measured solely by one's ability to pay for food, rent and transport, but should also account for healthcare, communication, social participation, savings and protection against financial shocks.

items.title: #NSTviral: F1 race over, but memories linger; Sepang clips captivate fans
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The race is long over, but Malaysian fans are still reliving Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia through "cinematic video clips" of cars speeding past Sepang's grandstands against an orange sunset. Videos circulating on Threads capture the evening atmosphere at Sepang International Circuit, with the fading sunlight and haze lending the event a movie-like quality. One video posted by user @mxrul drew more than 42,500 likes and 311,000 views.

items.title: Ringgit opens marginally higher against US dollar as 2027 Budget fiscal outlook in focus
items.summary: At 8am, the ringgit edged higher to 4.0880/0945 against the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0890/0940. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said markets would focus on the government's fiscal position, with expectations that it would maintain fiscal discipline and keep the fiscal deficit on a downward trajectory. Against regional currencies, the ringgit traded mixed.

items.title: Haze crisis worsens as unhealthy API readings force sweeping school closures in Putrajaya, Selangor and Rompin
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 9 — All education institutions under the Education Ministry (MOE) in the Federal Territory of Putrajaya and Selangor have been instructed to close today due to the haze. Meanwhile, in SHAH ALAM, Selangor state education director Datin Wan Nor Ashikin Abu Kassim confirmed the closure of all MOE education institutions in the state tomorrow, while Selangor Islamic Religious Department director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad announced in a separate statement also announced that all state religious schools under the department would be fully closed tomorrow, and recommended that private religious schools registered with the department to follow suit. In PAHANG, the state education department issued a statement tonight instructing education institutions under its purview in Rompin district to close tomorrow.

items.title: RTD uncovers fake international driving permits with bogus online verification system
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Fake International Driving Permits (IDPs) sold to foreigners for up to RM500 have come under scrutiny after authorities uncovered documents linked to websites designed to make them appear legitimate. Kuala Lumpur Road Transport Department (RTD) director Hamidi Adam said the department had detected parties offering documents purported to be IDPs to foreigners despite doubts over their validity under Malaysian law. Hamidi said foreigners who purchased the documents could mistakenly believe they were legally entitled to drive in Malaysia.

items.title: Shares slip as oil jumps and bond yields stay high
items.summary: Wall Street's main indexes fell, with the S&P 500 down about 0.5 per cent and the Nasdaq off nearly 1.3 per cent. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes , also pulled back from its elevated levels, dipping 5 basis points to 5.227 per cent. Overnight in Asia, Japan's Nikkei had shed 1.4 per cent and South Korea's chipmaker-heavy KOSPI slumped 2.6 per cent.

items.title: Hurricane Isaias strengthens to Cat 2 en route to southern US
items.summary: MIAMI: Hurricane Isaias intensified to Category 2 in the Gulf of Mexico's warm waters on Thursday as it churned towards the southern United States, the National Hurricane Centre (NHC) said. The first hurricane of the Atlantic season, Isaias is forecast to make landfall in Florida, Alabama or Mississippi overnight from Friday to Saturday, according to the NHC. Isaias comes unusually late as the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, which began on June 1.

items.title: Johor police chief: Civilian injured in shooting involving officer near Johor Zoo
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 9 — Police have confirmed that a shooting incident involving a policeman and a member of the public took place near the Johor Zoo along Jalan Gertak Merah here yesterday. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the individual was injured in the incident. “Johor police will hold a media conference regarding the incident tomorrow (today),” he said briefly when contacted by the media yesterday.

items.title: Anwar to table 2027 Budget at 3.30pm today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will table the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat at 3.30pm today. The tabling marks the fifth budget under his Madani Government, anchored by a commitment to ensure high-value growth translates equitably into the people's well-being while strengthening national economic resilience. As the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), it continues to pursue the three Madani Economy pillars: raising the growth ceiling, raising the living standards floor, and driving public administration governance reforms.

items.title: Trump says comment that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles was misinterpreted
items.summary: UNITED STATES: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said comments he made suggesting Iran could "take out" California cities had been misinterpreted, and that he was instead referring to the need for people to tolerate higher petrol prices. "It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. Let 'em take out Los Angeles, let 'em take out San Diego.

items.title: Trump administration to launch new vaccine research centre
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr., a vaccine sceptic, on Thursday announced a series of initiatives to study rare adverse effects of vaccines. "We must listen to patients and families who report vaccine injuries – not dismiss or gaslight them," Kennedy said in a statement announcing the creation of a research centre dedicated to monitoring and addressing vaccine side effects. Serious adverse effects remain very rare and are subject to continuous monitoring by health officials to ensure that the benefits of vaccines outweigh the risks.

items.title: From student hunger to bigger Sara aid, what could Budget 2027 have in store for Malaysians?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — All eyes will be on Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as he tables Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat this afternoon. Anwar’s fifth national Budget since taking office in 2022 comes amid growing speculation over an early 16th general election (GE16), raising expectations that it could be an election-year spending plan. Household finances, wages and social assistance are expected to feature prominently, although the extent of the government’s commitments will only become clear when Anwar delivers his Budget speech.

items.title: AI Nation 2030 push: Ministry of Digital offers 100,000 Coursera licences via Rakyat Digital
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Ministry of Digital, through MyDigital Corporation, is providing 100,000 learning licences to enable Malaysians to access digital and artificial intelligence (AI) courses through the online learning platform, Coursera. MyDigital Corporation said the initiative forms part of the Rakyat Digital ecosystem and supports the Malaysia Digital 2030 Action Plan (MD2030) and National AI Action Plan 2026-2030, in line with Malaysia’s AI Nation 2030 ambition. Meanwhile, Ministry of Digital Secretary-General Datuk Fabian Bigar said the initiative reflects the ministry’s commitment to making AI and digital learning accessible across all segments of society.

items.title: Schools in Malaysia to close from tomorrow if haze index tops 180, Education Ministry says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Schools and educational institutions under the Education Ministry in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 180 must close from tomorrow (October 9), as authorities step up measures to protect students and teachers from the worsening haze. Schools in areas where API readings remain above 150 for three consecutive days must also close from Monday, October 12, the ministry said in a statement today. “Areas recording API readings above 150 continuously for three consecutive days must close from Monday, October 12, 2026.”

items.title: Form Two boy injured after alleged beating by Form Four student at Kuala Pilah hostel
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Oct 8 — A Form Two male student was injured after allegedly being beaten by a Form Four student at a secondary school hostel in this district on September 27. Kuala Pilah District Police Chief Supt Muhammad Mustafah Hussin said the incident is believed to have taken place at about 11.40pm in one of the school’s hostels. The victim was then taken to Hospital Tuanku Ampuan Najihah for treatment,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Budget 2027: PM Anwar hopes to strengthen economy, ease rakyat’s burden
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim hopes Budget 2027, to be tabled tomorrow, will further strengthen the national economy while easing the burden on the people. Earlier, Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, inspected the final preparations for the Fifth Madani Budget at the Finance Ministry (MoF) in Putrajaya today ahead of its tabling in the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow. Anwar is scheduled to table Budget 2027 at 3.30pm.

items.title: ‘Ma, I love you… Bye Raa’: Zara Qairina’s tender voice echoes in court as mother breaks down
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 8 — Emotions ran high in the Coroner’s Court here today as the cheerful voice of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir, speaking affectionately to her mother, echoed through the courtroom during the inquest into the Form One student’s death. A total of 42 audio recordings were submitted as evidence, 35 of which captured conversations between Zara Qairina and her mother while the teenager was still alive. Throughout the recordings, Zara Qairina could be heard speaking cheerfully and affectionately as she shared various aspects of her daily life with her mother.

items.title: Budget 2027: Anwar to announce cheaper KTM Southern Shuttle fares, says Loke
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to announce good news regarding an initiative to make the KTM Komuter Southern Shuttle service more affordable during the tabling of the Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow. He said that the Southern Shuttle, launched in June, has so far transported approximately 20,000 passengers, averaging between 200 and 300 passengers daily. Loke had previously said that Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) utilises existing trains to operate the Southern Shuttle service, which connects Kulai to Johor Bahru Sentral, as well as Kempas Baru, Pasir Gudang and Paloh.

items.title: Families of 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal floods welcome 45‑day declaration proposal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — A proposal by Nepal to shorten the period for declaring disaster missing persons dead from 12 years to 45 days has brought relief to families of 54 Malaysians still missing after the flood tragedy there. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (Masfih) welcomed the proposal, describing it as a major relief for the 54 families facing emotional and financial strain 44 days after the tragedy. Masfih spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said all the families hoped the proposed provision could be implemented immediately to provide clarity for the next of kin of Malaysians still missing following the landslide and floods along the Nepal China border on Aug 26.

items.title: ‘Tonto’ pleads not guilty to 55 bribery charges totalling RM62,900 involving traffic police
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — A ‘tonto’ (lookout) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to 55 charges of giving RM62,900 in bribes to three traffic police officers between January 2022 and February 2026. According to the charges, the man was alleged to have corruptly given money to three traffic police officers from the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters, Negeri Sembilan Contingent Police Headquarters and the Kesas Expressway EMPV Patrol Office, as an inducement for them not to inspect lorries during roadblocks. The bribes were allegedly given in several transactions at several bank branches in Klang and Setia Alam, involving amounts ranging from RM700 to RM2,000.

items.title: Malaysia, Myanmar agree ministries must act together on refugee cooperation, says PM Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia and Myanmar agree that relevant ministries and agencies need to take coordinated and proactive action to advance bilateral cooperation, including efforts to address the issue of Myanmar refugees in Malaysia. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was emphasised during his meeting and bilateral talks with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing today. He said following their joint press conference, he and Min Aung Hlaing attended the Malaysia-Myanmar Cooperation Dialogue at Kompleks Seri Perdana, organised by the Institute of Strategic and International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia.

items.title: NRD issues 169,346 new generation MyKads nationwide in three weeks
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 8 — The National Registration Department (NRD) has issued a total of 169,346 New Generation MyKads nationwide between September 17 and October 6. NRD Director-General Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias said the five states recording the highest issuance are the Federal Territories with 20,592 pieces; Johor (18,871); Sarawak (15,777); Sabah (13,711) and Selangor (13,452). Also present was Terengganu NRD Director Awatif Hannan Md Yusup.

items.title: Anthony Loke: RTS Link not delayed, buffer time needed for safety approvals
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 8 — Malaysia and Singapore jointly decided to start the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link operations in February 2027, rather than taking a unilateral step, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. The minister said the approvals involved Malaysia’s Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) and Singapore’s Land Transport Authority (LTA). He said RTS Link operations could start as early as January, but February was chosen to provide a buffer and ensure safety evaluation and technical approvals proceed smoothly.

items.title: SUV driver fined RM4,000 for tailing Zahid Hamidi’s police convoy on Kesas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — A property agent was fined RM4,000 by the Magistrates’ Court here today after pleading guilty to disobeying a police order by following the convoy escorting Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi yesterday. He subsequently paid the fine. Earlier, a video went viral showing an SUV driver following a police convoy escorting the Deputy Prime Minister from Kajang towards Sunway Medical Centre in Subang Jaya.

items.title: Malaysia must strengthen regional cooperation to ensure stable energy supply, says Akmal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia has highlighted the need to strengthen regional cooperation to ensure a stable and affordable energy supply, alongside efforts to accelerate the transition to low-carbon energy. In a statement, the Ministry of Economy said that the Azec collaboration complements the implementation of the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), including energy efficiency, renewable energy, green mobility, infrastructure development, and transition financing. Earlier, Akmal Nasrullah also held a bilateral meeting with Josh Wilson, the Deputy Climate Change and Energy Minister from Australia’s Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, focusing on energy supply security and gas supply between the two countries.

items.title: Kelantan warns: Dogs without anti‑rabies vaccination tags may be culled
items.summary: BACHOK, Oct 8 — Dogs without vaccination tags or that have not received anti-rabies vaccinations after April each year may be culled by local authorities in Kelantan to curb the risk of rabies transmission. State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said the provision is in line with the Kelantan Anti-rabies Vaccination Order, which requires owners to ensure their pet dogs are vaccinated between January and April every year. “This year, 21 dogs in Bachok have been vaccinated, while samples from another 20 dogs have been taken for rabies testing,” he said.
